segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he began to speak to them in parables:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a vat for the winepress, and built a watchtower. Then he leased it to tenants and went abroad.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: At the season he sent a slave to the tenants, to collect from the tenants a share of the vineyard’s fruit.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But they seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty-handed.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Again he sent them another slave; that one they struck on the head and treated shamefully.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: He sent another, and that one they killed; and so with many others, beating some and killing others.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: He still had one, a beloved son. He sent him to them last of all, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But those tenants said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So they seized him and killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: What will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy the tenants, and give the vineyard to others.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Have you not even read this scripture: ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the cornerstone;

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: this came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They were looking for a way to arrest him, but they feared the crowd, for they knew that he had told the parable against them. So they left him and went away.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they sent to him some of the Pharisees and of the Herodians, to trap him in what he said.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They came and said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and defer to no one, for you show no partiality but truly teach the way of God. Is it permitted to give the poll tax to Caesar or not? Should we give it or should we not?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why are you testing me? Bring me a denarius so that I can look at it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They brought one. And he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Whose image is this, and whose inscription?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Caesar’s.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Give back to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they were utterly amazed at him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Sadducees came to him, who say there is no resurrection, and they put a question to him:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man’s brother dies and leaves behind a wife but leaves no child, his brother should take the wife and raise up offspring for his brother.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: There were seven brothers. The first took a wife, and when he died he left no offspring.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: The second took her, and died leaving no offspring behind; and the third likewise.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: None of the seven left offspring. Last of all the woman died too.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: In the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife will she be? For all seven had her as wife.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Is this not why you are mistaken: that you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For when they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in the heavens.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And as for the dead, that they are raised: have you not read in the book of Moses, in the passage about the bush, how God spoke to him, saying, ‘I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob’?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: He is not God of the dead but of the living. You are badly mistaken.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of the scribes came up and heard them debating. Seeing that Jesus had answered them well, he asked him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Which commandment is first of all?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The first is: ‘Hear, Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The second is this: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The scribe said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Well said, Teacher. You have spoken truly: he is one, and there is no other besides him;

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: and to love him with all the heart and with all the understanding and with all the strength, and to love one’s neighbor as oneself, is far more than all the whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus, seeing that he had answered thoughtfully, said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You are not far from the kingdom of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And after that no one dared to question him any more.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While teaching in the temple, Jesus spoke up and said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “How can the scribes say that the Messiah is David’s son?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: David himself said, in the Holy Spirit, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet.”’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: David himself calls him Lord; so how can he be his son?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the large crowd was listening to him gladly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And in his teaching he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in long robes and to be greeted in the marketplaces,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: and to have the front seats in the synagogues and the places of honor at banquets.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: They devour widows’ houses and for show make long prayers. These will receive a harsher judgment.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Sitting down opposite the treasury, he watched how the crowd was putting money into the treasury. Many rich people were putting in large amounts.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then one poor widow came and put in two tiny coins, together worth a quadrans.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Calling his disciples to him, he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those who are putting into the treasury.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For they all put in out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty put in everything she had, all she had to live on.”

notes.note: The fence, the winepress vat and the tower echo the song of the vineyard in Isaiah 5:1–7, where the vineyard is Israel and its owner is God. Hearers who knew that passage would have recognised the picture at once and taken the tenants to be those entrusted with Israel. Absentee owners leasing land to tenants for a share of the crop was a familiar arrangement.

The Greek word means a person owned by a master, not a hired employee. Most older English versions soften it to 'servant'; several recent ones use 'slave'. In the Septuagint the prophets are called God's slaves, which is probably part of the parable's point.

This form of the verb is found nowhere else in surviving Greek, so its meaning has to be inferred from its evident connection with the word for 'head' and from the context. 'Struck on the head' is the usual understanding, but the precise sense is uncertain. Later manuscripts add that the tenants stoned him.

The quotation is Psalm 118:22–23 in its Greek form. The phrase is literally 'head of the corner' and may mean either a foundation stone at the corner of a building or the stone that crowns it, such as a capstone. Scholars are divided; either way it is the most important stone, and the builders had rejected it.

The word is borrowed from Latin census and refers to the head tax Rome levied on Judea after it came under direct Roman rule in AD 6, payable in Roman coin. Its introduction had provoked an armed revolt, and it remained a symbol of subjection. A plain yes would discredit Jesus with the crowd; a plain no could be reported as sedition.

The questioners asked whether to 'give' the tax; Jesus answers with a compound verb that means to give back or pay what is owed. 'Render' once said this but is now obscure. The coin bears Caesar's image and so is treated as his; many interpreters hear an unstated counterpart, that people bear God's image, but the text does not say so.
The Greek is plural, a Semitic turn of phrase for God's dwelling that this translation keeps where it occurs. Most translations flatten it to 'heaven'.

notes.phrase: in the passage about the bush
notes.note: The Greek says only 'at the bush'. Before chapter and verse numbers existed, a passage was cited by its subject; this is the burning bush account in Exodus 3. The Sadducees are answered from the books of Moses, which they themselves had quoted as their authority.

notes.phrase: the Lord our God, the Lord is one
notes.traditional: The Lord our God is one Lord
notes.note: This is Deuteronomy 6:4, the opening of the Shema, the confession devout Jews recited daily. The Greek, like the Hebrew behind it, can also be read 'the Lord our God is one Lord' or 'the Lord is our God, the Lord alone'. The rendering here follows the scribe's own summary in verse 32, 'he is one'.

The Greek word means 'anointed one' and here is a title for the king Israel expected, not a name for Jesus. 'Messiah' conveys the title to a modern reader, while 'Christ' is kept where the word functions as a name. Several modern translations make the same distinction.

notes.phrase: The Lord said to my Lord
notes.note: The quotation is Psalm 110:1. In Hebrew the first 'Lord' is the divine name and the second is an ordinary word for a superior, 'my lord'; the Greek version uses the same word for both. The argument assumes that David is the speaker and that the one he addresses is the Messiah, so that David calls his own descendant his superior.

notes.phrase: two tiny coins, together worth a quadrans
notes.traditional: two mites, which make a farthing
notes.note: The lepton was the smallest coin in circulation in Judea. Mark explains its value in Roman terms for his readers: two made one quadrans, the smallest Roman coin, a sixty-fourth of a denarius, and a denarius was roughly a day's wage for a laborer. Renderings such as 'penny' or 'farthing' give the general idea but no real sense of the amount.

It ranges over 'life', 'self' and 'soul' across the New Testament, and 'soul' can import later ideas of an immaterial part of a person, so the senses need a single policy.
Jesus' distinctive opening formula occurs dozens of times in all four Gospels and is variously rendered 'truly', 'verily', 'amen' and 'I assure you'.
'Scribe' suggests a copyist to modern readers whereas the word denotes a trained expert in the Law, and translations vary between 'scribe', 'teacher of the law' and 'legal expert'.
The same verb covers 'test' and 'tempt' across the Gospels and letters, and English versions switch between them in ways that hide the connection.
